transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-04
Time: 15:00 PT | Duration: ~48 mins
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Brooks (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Orion VP Product), Carlos Mendes (Orion SRE), Aisha Khan (Orion Head Compliance)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE for the Orion account. Liam, do you want to intro quickly?
[00:10] Liam: Yeah hi all, Liam Brooks, SE. We'll walk through the Console usage views and per-route cost breakdown, and then surface Optimize recs for lowering unit cost. Feel free to jump in with questions.
[00:24] Priya: Thanks, excited — we want to understand how usage maps to cost across our different routes, and whether we can keep latency under 100ms for critical user flows.
[00:35] Carlos: Also, we'd like to see retention settings and where logs live, and how that ties to compliance.
[00:42] Aisha: Hi, and I want to verify encryption, KMS, SSO, and audit trace capabilities.

--- Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect) ---
Summary: Quick Console walkthrough focused on usage analytics, route-level cost, Optimize suggestions (batching, quantization), Dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, and security requirements (SOC2, KMS, SSO). Next steps: Redwood to send pricing and route CSV export, Orion to confirm pilot routes.

[01:08] Liam: OK I'm sharing my screen — heading to Console > Usage > Routes. You can see at the top we have a summary line for the org: total tokens, total generated, average latency, and cost. I'm going to filter to the last 30 days.
[01:32] [Liam clicks] 
[01:35] Liam: Here you can toggle between 'per-call' and 'per-token' cost, and group by route or model. For Orion, we see three obvious routes: conversation-v1, search-embed, and summary-svc. Right now conversation-v1 is 64% of spend but only 40% of token volume — meaning it's high unit cost, likely due to long generation sequences or a larger model.
[01:58] Priya: Could that be because of our system prompt and long context windows? We do send full customer histories sometimes.
[02:06] Liam: Yep, that tracks. Console flags routes with long seq length distribution. If you click into the route detail we show sequence length histogram and prefix reuse — that's where the KV cache comes in.
[02:20] Carlos: Quick question: KV cache? We use Redis for a few things — is the KV cache internal to Redwood runtime or do we need to manage it?
[02:30] Liam: KV cache is internal caching of key-value activations on the GPU runtime — reduces repeated prefix compute. Sometimes the transcripting shows "KV cash" or similar, apologies for auto-captions. For Orion, we see about 18% cache hit on conversation-v1; optimizing prompts & prefix caching can cut tokens by ~15-30% depending on reuse.
[02:53] Priya: Nice. Do you show token-level cost breakdown? We want to chargeback to product teams.
[03:00] Liam: Yes, per-route dashboards include token_count, per_token_rate, and aggregated cost. You can export CSV for route-level chargeback. I'll share a sample export after the call.

[03:18] Maya: Quick aside — from a pricing perspective, if you move those heavy routes to Dedicated capacity you get predictable throughput and lower per-token price at scale; Dedicated also allows pinning model versions. We can run a cost projection for your 3-month forecast.
[03:36] Priya: Any lock-in? We prefer to keep the flexibility to use hosted for spikes and dedicated for steady traffic.
[03:44] Maya: That's a common pattern — we support hybrid routing. Console's routing policy lets you define primary as Dedicated and fallback to Hosted or a lower-cost variant. There are also autoscale and burst policies.

[04:00] [04:00] Liam: Back to the UI, clicking 'Optimize suggestions' on the route shows we recommend: enable auto-batching for conversation-v1 with a 40ms batch window, enable prefix caching for similar request types, and consider int8 quantization for the model used on summary-svc. Each recommendation shows estimated savings and potential latency impact.
[04:30] Carlos: How do you estimate those savings? Is it heuristic or based on historical runs?
[04:37] Liam: It's hybrid — we use historical telemetry from the route if available, bucketed by seq length and model, then apply our runtime throughput/latency models. For cold routes we use profile-based estimates. We also surface confidence bands.
[04:53] Aisha: On quantization — are there accuracy regressions? Our summaries are legally sensitive; we need quality preserved.
[05:01] Liam: Good question. We recommend evaluating with a small eval prompt set; Redwood Optimize integrates with your evals so you can run A/B and see delta in ROUGE or other metrics. We also show example prompts that are more sensitive to quantization.
[05:16] Priya: That integration — is that part of the hosted Console or an add-on?
[05:21] Maya: Optimize is an add-on/tier feature. For pilots we often enable it for 30 days to tune quant profiles and batching.

[05:34] [05:34] Liam: Showing route timeline now — usage spikes at 09:00 UTC and 18:00 UTC, aligning with Orion's Europe and US traffic. You can set alerts on cost per day or latency percentiles.
[05:52] Priya: Can we break down cost by team? Our product has multiple subteams calling the same route; we need accurate chargeback.
[06:00] Liam: If you pass a team-specific header or attribute in the API call we can group by header and report per-team. There's also token-level attribution by API key.
[06:11] Carlos: Do you support service accounts + SSO for team separation?
[06:16] Maya: Yes, we support SSO/SAML and RBAC for the Console, and you can provision service keys scoped to routes. Audit logs show key usage. Aisha, you'll like that — we also persist audit logs to S3 or a customer-managed bucket if you've chosen Private deployment.
[06:34] Aisha: Can audit logs be filtered for only metadata and not full-payload? We have regs requiring that full PII never leaves our environment.
[06:42] Liam: We have log redaction features; you can choose to strip or hash PII fields. For Private deployments you can also opt to never store full request bodies in Redwood logs.

[07:00] Priya: Back on costs — you mentioned per-route caching and batch windows. How much does batching increase latency tail?
[07:08] Liam: Depends on batch time window and load. For high QPS routes, batching often *reduces* latency because better GPU utilization avoids queuing. For low QPS, batching waits can add ms; Optimize suggests per-route batch window and shows estimated p95 impact.
[07:26] Carlos: For Dedicated, do you guarantee p95 latency?
[07:31] Maya: Our SLA specifies availability and target latency bands for certain Dedicated SKUs; we can include p95 tail targets in the contract. If you need strict guarantees we recommend Dedicated with isolation.

[07:45] Liam: I'm switching to the 'Cost Explorer' — you can break down by model family. Interesting to note: conversation-v1 uses a 70B model by default in your traffic, summary-svc uses a 13B variant. That aligns with the high unit cost on conversation.
[08:06] Priya: Can we route conversation-v1 to a cheaper 30B variant for non-critical flows?
[08:12] Liam: Absolutely — Console supports route-level model variants and rollout policies. You can do canary traffic percentages and automatic rollback on quality regressions (if you plug your evals).
[08:23] Maya: We also have a cost-sensitivity toggle — if a route exceeds a cost threshold the policy can fallback to a smaller model automatically.

[08:36] [08:36] Carlos: Let's talk private deployments briefly — what's the difference between Private and Dedicated?
[08:44] Maya: Dedicated is a tenant-isolated pool managed by Redwood in our cloud. Private is either VPC-hosted control plane + customer-managed networking or fully on-prem. Private is for stricter compliance or data residency; it includes options for KMS/HSM integration and non-extractable logs.
[08:59] Aisha: Do you have SOC2 docs and an ISO cert?
[09:04] Maya: We maintain SOC 2 Type II — I'll attach the latest report. We also have an ISO 27001 attestation in process; I will share the SOC2 link after the call.
[09:15] Aisha: We also need contract language around data retention, right-to-erasure, and audit access.
[09:21] Maya: We have standard clauses and can scope retention windows per customer. For pilot projects we often set a short live retention and turn on redaction.

[09:34] Liam: Back to Optimize recs — for conversation-v1 the Console shows: (1) enable per-route caching for conversation context, (2) reduce model to 30B for non-critical endpoints, (3) add prompt compression via tokenizers (we have examples), (4) enable int8 quantization for 13B models. Estimated savings: 28-42% in monthly spend for the route depending on adoption.
[10:02] Priya: The tokenizer compression examples — are they automated or manual changes?
[10:07] Liam: We provide a small library and examples to rewrite prompts. Some customers automate prompt compaction in middleware, others rely on our pre-processing rules.
[10:16] Carlos: Is the real-time pre-processing safe for PII?
[10:20] Liam: It can run either in your stack or in Redwood's runtime; for PII you should run client-side or in your VPC.

[10:34] [10:34] Maya: I want to demo the route-level alerting quick — you can set a spend threshold and a p95 latency threshold. Also the Console allows scheduled reports emailed to stakeholders which Orion asked about.
[10:50] Priya: Good — we need weekly cost summaries for product and infra.
[10:54] Maya: We'll set up a template and share it.

[11:05] Liam: Quick detour on benchmarking — if Orion wants to run performance tests we'll need a small pilot account and a list of representative prompts. We can run a head-to-head on your traffic profile between hosted and Dedicated. That helps fine-tune batch windows and autoscale settings.
[11:24] Priya: Sounds good. What sort of lead time for a pilot?
[11:28] Maya: Typically 2–4 weeks to set up tests and get initial numbers. For Private on-prem it'd be longer, depending on infra.

[11:40] Carlos: Regarding logs export — can we stream audit logs to our SIEM?
[11:45] Liam: Yes, we support streaming to popular SIEMs, or direct S3 export; logs can be filtered and redacted per your policy.

[12:00] Aisha: A few compliance specific questions: do you support customer-managed KMS?
[12:05] Maya: Yes, for Private we support customer KMS/HSM integration; for Hosted we support BYOK in select regions. I'll note to include specifics in the security pack we send.

[12:18] [12:18] Priya: On pricing — do you have an example of how a hybrid routing cost looks month-to-month?
[12:24] Maya: I'll run a 3-month projection based on your historical token volume. It will show a blended per-token rate if you route some % to Dedicated and the rest to Hosted. I'll include the math in the spreadsheet.

[12:34] Liam: Small demo of exporting diagnostics — clicking 'Export route CSV' now; see fields: timestamp, api_key_alias, route, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, cost_usd. That CSV can feed your internal billing pipeline.
[12:53] Carlos: Perfect. That's what we need.

[13:05] [13:05] Priya: One more question — you mentioned automatic rollbacks on quality when rollouts go wrong. How is quality measured?
[13:13] Liam: There are two ways: integrate your eval set and Redwood will compute metrics for A/B; or set heuristics (like prompt-specific checks). For text generation we support diff-based checks, and for embeddings you can check vector-sim thresholds.

[13:33] Maya: We're approaching 30 minutes in — do we want to walk through a quick hypothetical cost-savings example for conversation-v1?
[13:40] Priya: Yes please.

[13:43] Liam: OK I toggle on a scenario: enable auto-batching, compress prompts by 12% on average, reduce model for 20% of traffic, and enable prefix caching to increase hit-rate to 45%. That gives an estimated 35% cost reduction and p95 changes in the single-digit ms for most traffic. These numbers are in the screenshot.
[14:08] Priya: That looks promising. Any caveats?
[14:12] Liam: Main caveats: need to validate user visible quality for the 20% traffic moved to smaller model; quantization needs evaluation; and batch windows need to be tuned for your QPS pattern.

[14:26] Carlos: For the pilot we should keep a control group and measure key metrics like response correctness, latency percentiles, and cost.
[14:33] Maya: Agreed. That's precisely the pilot scope we propose.

[14:40] [14:40] Aisha: On regulation — if we do Private, can we ensure logs never leave our VPC?
[14:46] Liam: In Private on-prem or VPC control plane we can ensure logs stay in your S3 bucket and don't ship to Redwood-managed storage. We'll document the guarantees.

[15:00] Priya: Good. Let's talk timeline and next steps.
[15:05] Maya: Proposed next steps: 1) Redwood sends Dedicated pilot pricing and sample contract language, 2) Redwood shares the route CSV export and benchmarking checklist (SE will run an initial profiling), 3) Orion confirms two pilot routes and objectives (cost reduction % and latency SLO).
[15:28] Priya: We'll aim to pick pilot routes by end of next Tuesday.
[15:32] Maya: Great. Any last questions?
[15:35] Carlos: One more — do you have examples of customers who did route-level chargeback?
[15:40] Maya: Yes, we've done it for a few mid-market customers — I'll share a sanitized example spreadsheet.

[15:46] Aisha: Also, please include the SOC2 report and the redaction matrix.
[15:50] Maya: Will do.

[15:58] Liam: Alright I'm going to drop the links in chat: 1) Console route export sample CSV (link), 2) Dedicated pricing template (link), 3) Optimize pilot guide (link).
[16:12] Maya: Thanks everyone — quick recap: we'll send pricing + security docs, SE will share CSV export and benchmark plan, Orion to confirm pilot routes and metrics.

[16:24] Priya: Thanks, that was helpful.
[16:27] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up via CRM with artifacts and proposed dates.
